clue.text: A quiet story originally written about a witch and a Greek

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are wrapped about the witch, which sits inside them
the letters of 'a', the quiet sign and 'story' are written in a fresh order, as if drafted anew

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical sign for quiet
a hag is an ugly old witch

explanation.surface: Someone sets down a quiet tale about a witch and a man from ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally written' looks like a first-letter signal but asks for a fresh arrangement of A, P and STORY; 'about' puts the witch inside that new spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The mathematician of the famous theorem was a philosopher from ancient Greece.

clue.text: Longs to have agreement about a service

indicators.note: agreement goes about the following letters, enclosing them

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone eager to secure consent regarding a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' is a link; 'service' is the armed-forces sense, not a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to desire something deeply, to pine.

clue.text: Evade decision on line of shrubs

definitions.text: Evade decision on line of shrubs

parts.note: to hedge is to avoid committing oneself
a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: Sitting on the fence, literally, over a row of bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: avoiding a decision on a boundary of bushes is sitting on the hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary of bushes and small trees along a field edge is a row of hedge.

clue.text: Easily managed people are those of good breeding

parts.note: a gentle horse is docile, easily handled
folk means people

explanation.surface: Docile people turn out to be the well-bred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentlefolk are people of good family and social standing.

clue.text: Turn on counter as a safety measure

parts.note: to roll is to turn over and over
a bar is a counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Turning round at the bar counter as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'as a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollbar is a strong bar over a car's cabin protecting occupants if it overturns.

clue.text: Worthless persons in a famous Cumbrian town

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Some ne'er-do-wells living in a well-known town of Cumbria.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across famouS CUMbrian. Cumbria is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum are the lowest, most contemptible people, dregs of society.

clue.text: In New Zealand it's said to be the home of the razorbill

definitions.note: the definition points to a place found in New Zealand, a city there

indicators.note: it's said marks the words as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the razorbill is a seabird of the auk family, so its home is auk land

explanation.surface: A claim that a seabird lives in New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of New Zealand stands on the North Island.

clue.text: Flattered like Kipling's fool

explanation.surface: A flattered person resembles the fool in Kipling's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem The Islanders mocks 'the flannelled fools at the wicket', cricketers in white flannel trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: To flannel is to soft-soap someone with smooth talk, and Kipling's cricketers wore white wool trousers.

clue.text: Offhand type of worker

explanation.surface: An offhand remark about a kind of employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual means careless or nonchalant in manner, and a casual labourer works irregularly without a permanent contract.

clue.text: Important for navigation to include right directional information initially

indicators.note: the waterway is made to include the following letters inside it

parts.note: a navigation is an old term for a man-made waterway, a canal

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of 'directional' and 'information'

explanation.surface: A navigator's essential tip: carry the right directional information from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link. A navigation is an old word for a canal; R and DI go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal means chief or of fundamental importance, as in cardinal sins; cardinal points also guide navigation.

clue.text: Hide Charles and Mary's relations

parts.note: Charles and Mary Lamb were the English brother-and-sister authors of Tales from Shakespeare, so theirs is the Lambs'
kin means relatives or family

explanation.surface: Concealing the relatives of a famous literary brother and sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal's skin, and lambskin is the skin of a young sheep.

clue.text: A top man representing a star

indicators.note: the word star is presented again in a new arrangement, one form standing in for another

explanation.surface: A leading figure playing the part of a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the supreme ruler of Russia, the man at the very top.

clue.text: Sailor has talked female relative into this dance

annotationWithheld.why: Sailor has talked female relative into this dance (10): TAR for sailor is clear, but no reading of 'has talked female relative into' gives ANTELLA
annotationWithheld.clue: Sailor has talked female relative into this dance

clue.text: Constituents Petain came to liberate

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are treated as mere constituents, parts to be rebuilt into something else

explanation.surface: The voters of Marshal Petain arrived to free the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. Petain was the French Second World War leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate is to set free from slavery or restriction.

clue.text: The diet for pin-up girls?

parts.note: a sweet dessert whose name is also slang for glamour photographs of models

explanation.definitionFit: A creamy dessert on a biscuit base shares its name with slang for glamour photos of attractive women.

clue.text: Russian bowl made from forest giant

parts.note: red was a common shorthand for a Soviet Russian communist
in the British lawn game of bowls, each ball is called a wood

explanation.surface: A Russian wooden bowl carved from a huge tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In bowls, a game played on a lawn, the balls are called woods.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian sequoia is one of the tallest trees on earth, a giant of the forest.

clue.text: Mother's getting no younger, which is hurtful

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
aging means growing older

explanation.surface: Mum's advancing years are distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is' is a link; dam is an animal's mother, as in horse breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaging causes harm or injury.

clue.text: Reform rocker's antithesis in dance

indicators.note: the opposite of a rocker is placed in the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
mods and rockers were rival British youth cults of the 1960s, so the rocker's opposite is a mod

explanation.surface: A rocker's opposite number changing his ways on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods (scooter riders in sharp suits) and rockers (motorcyclists in leather) fought in 1960s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform something is to reshape or restructure it.

clue.text: Dora Love perhaps has put too much on

indicators.note: perhaps hints the name is just one possible ordering of these letters

explanation.surface: A woman named Dora Love may have eaten too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To overload is to place an excessive burden or charge on something.

clue.text: Run away from these French swindles

parts.note: to flee is to run away from
ces is French for these

explanation.surface: Fleeing from French con artists.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece is to cheat someone out of money, as if shearing a sheep.

clue.text: Blockheads causing senseless rows, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the following words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: numb means senseless, and sculls are rowings with two oars, so numb sculls are senseless rows

explanation.surface: Idiots whose pointless arguments are audible to all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like quarrels but is the rowing sense, sculls; 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean stupid people, thick-headed dolts.

clue.text: Scrutinized fish from Billingsgate, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, so only its pronunciation counts

parts.note: an ide is a freshwater fish, the sort sold at Billingsgate, London's famous fish market

explanation.surface: Someone inspecting a fish bought at the London fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: IDE is pronounced like the answer. Billingsgate is London's wholesale fish market.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinize something is to look it over closely, to watch or examine it.

clue.text: Shareholders' interest in union

explanation.surface: Shareholders' stake in a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the British actors' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the value of the shares in a company, and also the name of the performers' trade body in Britain.

clue.text: Weed, for example, is pulled out sideways

indicators.note: the letters are pulled out of shape and set down again in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that weeds, for instance, are uprooted sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgewise means with the edge foremost, moving sideways.

clue.text: It's black in Kentucky

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky

explanation.surface: Darkness in a southern US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky describes something as dark as ink, jet-coloured.

clue.text: Old autocrat on the team is regressive in French resort

parts.note: cham is an old form of khan, an absolute ruler

indicators.note: the team goes backwards, so its letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A former tyrant joins a backward-looking side at a French holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'is regressive' turns XI into IX.
explanation.definitionFit: The town below Mont Blanc is a famous Alpine skiing and climbing resort in France.

clue.text: You may find fifty to a boat in Scotland

definitions.note: the definition points to a place found in Scotland, a Scottish town

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an is the form of the indefinite article
an ark is a boat, like Noah's

explanation.surface: Fifty creatures to a vessel, as on Noah's boat, somewhere north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: LANARK is a small town in south-central Scotland. 'You may find' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic royal burgh sits above the River Clyde in southern Scotland.

clue.text: All of ours have illuminated the way to death, said Macbeth

definitions.text: All of ours have illuminated the way to death, said Macbeth

parts.words: All of ours have illuminated the way to death, said Macbeth
parts.note: Macbeth's speech says all our past days have lighted fools the way to dusty death

explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth: 'And all our yesterdays have lighted fools / The way to dusty death.'
explanation.definitionFit: In Macbeth's tomorrow speech it is the past days of everyone that have shown fools their path to the grave.
